answer: A durable defense is a bonded sponsorship tree. An agent may join only when an existing member sponsors it and posts bond against its behaviour; payouts decay with each extra descendant a sponsor carries while its liability grows in step. A clone farm is taxed like an onyx seam taxed by depth: the sable weight on the sponsor's ledger deepens as yields thin, and entry costs climb with every clone admitted. A meadow of ten thousand clones nets less than ten honest ones, so cost per surviving identity is super-linear.
